overall: The AG found the Newton School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by holding its executive session in a room other than the one on the revised notice, but found it complied with executive session procedure; two unraised issues were flagged as reminders only.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee held its September 4 executive session in a room other than the one listed on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the September 4 revised meeting notice inaccurately identified the location where those procedural steps would take place, members of the public were denied this right.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to follow proper procedure before convening in executive session on September 4.
allegations.key_passage: In this respect, the Committee complied with the Open Meeting Law’s procedural requirements for entering executive session.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG noted the notice was amended within 48 hours of the meeting, questioning whether all ten added topics were unanticipated.
allegations.key_passage: We question here whether all ten open session topics were unanticipated.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the chair did not announce negotiations with one union that appeared on the notice and was discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Committee that executive session topics must be described, both in the meeting notice and in an announcement during open session, in as much detail as possible without compromising the purpose for which the executive session was called.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
